chapter_name: Colonialism and the Countryside: Exploring Official Archives
learning_objective: 📜 Discover how British colonial policies devastated Indian agriculture, the rise of powerful moneylenders, and the fierce tribal rebellions against the East India Company!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793. The East India Company fixed the land revenue forever. Zamindars were made owners of the land as long as they paid the tax. If they failed to pay before sunset on a specific day (Sunset Law), their estates were auctioned off.

While Zamindars lived in cities and struggled to pay high taxes, rich peasants called 'Jotedars' consolidated power in the villages. They controlled local trade, lent money, and deliberately delayed tax payments to ruin the Zamindars.

main_concepts.concept_title: ⛏️ The Hoe vs. The Plough (Rajmahal Hills)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Paharias lived in the hills, practicing shifting agriculture with a 'hoe' (symbol of their lifestyle). The British encouraged the Santhals to settle at the base of the hills, clear forests, and use the 'plough' for settled agriculture, leading to conflict.

The Santhals were given a designated land called 'Damin-i-Koh'. However, they soon realized they were being crushed by heavy British taxes and corrupt moneylenders (dikus). In 1855, they rose in a massive, bloody rebellion against the British.

In western India, the British used the 'Ryotwari' system (taxing peasants directly). When the American Civil War ended, cotton prices crashed. Peasants, trapped in massive debt by moneylenders, rebelled in 1875 by burning account books (bahi khatas).

fun_activity.title: 🎭 The Fake Auction Trick
fun_activity.instructions: When a Zamindar's estate was auctioned under the Sunset Law, they used a clever trick! The Zamindar's own agents would bid the highest price to buy the land back. They would then refuse to pay the money, forcing another auction. They repeated this until the British gave up and sold it back to the original Zamindar for a tiny amount!

exam_tips: 📌 Ensure you can explain the shift of power from the urban Zamindar to the rural Jotedar in Bengal.
📌 Contrast the 'Hoe' (representing the shifting cultivation of the Paharias) with the 'Plough' (representing the settled agriculture of the Santhals).
📌 Explain why the Permanent Settlement revenue demand was initially set so high (because the British knew they could never increase it later).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Fifth Report was submitted to the British Parliament in 1813, highly critical of the East India Company's administration.
⭐ Francis Buchanan was a British physician who traveled through the Rajmahal hills and documented the landscape for the Company.
⭐ The American Civil War caused a temporary boom in Indian cotton exports, which collapsed disastrously when the war ended.
